newsitem.title: USA: K.C. Power, Western Resources extend merger talks.
newsitem.headline: K.C. Power, Western Resources extend merger talks.

text.p: Kansas City Power & Light Co. and Western Resources Inc. said Thursday that merger talks were continuing and that Western had extended its $1.9 billion offer for the utility for one more day.
Topeka, Kan.-based Western Resources, an electric and gas utility in Kansas and Oklahoma, has been pursuing Kansas City Power, based in Kansas City, Mo., since last April.

Western said in a statement that it was extending its tender offer to Friday due to positive dialogue between the two companies and the complexity of negotiations. The offer, extended several times before, was due to expire Thursday.
Western Resources in June raised its bid to $31 a share in Western stock for each Kansas City Power share, or about $1.9 billion, from $28 a share, or about $1.7 billion.
While Kansas City Power had initially rejected Western's bid, since late last year the two companies have been negotiating the terms of a merger or alliance.
If no agreement is reached, Western may try to force the issue by seeking to replace all or part of Kansas City Power's board at the annual shareholders' meeting this spring.
